## Why This Is Asked

This question evaluates the ability to apply advanced security controls to real-world CI/CD supply chains in multi-tenant environments, with emphasis on provenance verification, code signing, and rapid incident response.

## Key Concepts

- Software supply chain integrity
- Module provenance and signing (Sigstore/cosign)
- Pre-merge and runtime policy enforcement (OPA/Conftest)
- Drift detection and automated remediation
- Incident response planning and execution

## Code Example

```rego
package ci.supplychain
default allow = false

allow {
    input.provenance.verified
    input.provenance.signer == "trusted-module-owner"
    input.provenance.entry_point == "main.tf"
    not input.provenance.dependencies[_].untrusted
}

deny[msg] {
    not allow
    msg := "Module provenance verification failed"
}
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests SecOps of supply-chain risk and rapid containment in multi-tenant SaaS.

## Key Concepts
- Supply-chain security, SBOM, reproducible builds, attestation, canary deployment, rapid rollback.
- CI/CD hardening with Dependabot, SBOM scanning, and signed artifacts.
- Incident metrics: MTTR, RPO, RTO, blast radius.

## Code Example
```javascript
name: Build and attest
on: [push]
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Build
        run: npm ci && npm run build
      - name: SBOM
        run: syft packages dir:./dist -o cyclonedx | tee bom.xml
      - name: Sign
        run: cosign sign --key cosign.key ./dist
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you verify all tenants are protected during rollout and when to roll back?
- What if a compromised CI runner existed?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question probes advanced defense-in-depth for supply-chain risk, blending build-time SBOM governance with runtime attestation and automated policy enforcement. It also evaluates the candidate's understanding of multi-tenant security isolation and incident response workflows that minimize blast radius.

## Key Concepts
- Runtime attestation: Verifying container integrity before execution
- SBOM (Software Bill of Materials): Inventory of software components for vulnerability tracking
- Sigstore cosign: Open-source image signing and verification tool
- OPA Gatekeeper / Kyverno: Kubernetes admission controllers for policy enforcement
- CI SBOM integration: Automated artifact scanning during the build phase
- Per-tenant isolation: Namespace-level security boundaries in multi-tenant clusters
- Incident response playbooks: Structured procedures for rapid threat response

## Code Example
```rego
package kubernetes.admission

deny[msg] {
  input.review.kind.kind == "Pod"
  image := input.review.object.spec.containers[_].image
  not verified_image[image]
  msg := sprintf("Image '%v' is not signed or lacks a valid SBOM", [image])
}

verified_image[image] {
  cosign.verify(image)
  sbom_exists(image)
}

sbom_exists(image) {
  input.review.object.metadata.annotations["sbom.id"]
}
```

## Success Criteria
1. All production images are signed with cosign before registry admission
2. SBOM覆盖率 reaches 100% for critical workloads
3. Gatekeeper/Kyverno policies block 100% of unsigned images at admission time
4. Tenant namespaces are isolated with zero cross-tenant network access
5. IR playbook execution achieves containment within 1 hour of alert
